title: Sub-Scope Returned Package Import Delivery
summary: extend the sub-scope Import workflow with trusted returned-package overwrite, stale-source, and all-or-nothing protection
content_html:
Sub-Scope Returned Package Import Delivery

Status And Order

Delivered as SRR-2 after both the completed Sub-Scope Returned Package Review Delivery and completed Sub-Scope Ordinary Document Import Delivery.

SRR-1 proved that one complete returned package from an exact { scope, sub_scope } collection can reach faithful, immutable Docs Review. SSO-1 first establishes one exact-collection Import control and shared ordinary source target. SRR-2 then extends that workflow with one separately confirmed path from an eligible returned JSON/JSONL package back to the same canonical flat collection.

This is not a Save control in Docs Review and does not broaden ordinary scope-level Docs Import.

Complete Outcome

A local Manage docs_subscope report uses the compact 📥 Import icon and exact mounted-collection workflow introduced by SSO-1. SRR-2 adds trusted returned packages as a separate source type; it does not add a second report button. Scope-level and sub-scope package Import share one sequential package plan confirmation modal after the existing Import chooser.

The action:

  1. freezes the mounted { scope, sub_scope } collection;
  2. lists only trusted returned packages that match that exact collection and explicitly support return Import;
  3. previews one complete package against current canonical sources;
  4. requires one package-level confirmation;
  5. applies every accepted source update or none; and
  6. rebuilds and refreshes only the owning sub-scope projection.

Import is a collection action. It never consumes checked IDs, the displayed detail document, the parent report document, URL text, the latest staged file, or the package currently open in Docs Review.

Report Toolbar Contract

  • The 📥 button remains the one local management contribution introduced by SSO-1, with Import as its accessible label and title. Public reports receive no control, service probe, or Import module.
  • Import is a sibling toolbar control, not an item in the selection-owned Actions menu. Activating it does not enter selection mode, reveal checkboxes, or change checked IDs.
  • The existing 🔧 Actions control keeps its current behavior: opening it enters selection mode and Prepare package… remains checked-ID-backed.
  • Import availability remains independent of collection rows. SRR-2 adds package availability to the existing exact-collection Import surface without changing ordinary staged-source availability.
  • Activating the button lazily loads a focused sub-scope package workflow using the exact mounted collection and restores focus to the same button on close.
  • The package chooser shows file, configured collection label, and document count. It includes only packages whose trusted scope and sub_scope match the frozen collection and whose supports_return_import is true.
  • Preview collection remains in the existing Import chooser. A successful preview closes or hides that chooser before opening one shared package-plan confirmation modal; the modals are sequential and never nested.
  • Scope-level { scope } package Import and sub-scope { scope, sub_scope } package Import use that same confirmation modal and collection controller. Only their explicit validated target shapes differ.
  • The confirmation modal contains the complete reviewed plan and a visible fixed footer with only Cancel and Confirm import. There is no Back control: Cancel closes the complete Import workflow and applies nothing; choosing another package requires reopening Import.
  • No package is silently preselected from another route or workflow. Confirming Import always follows an explicit package choice and reviewed preview.
  • Cancel applies nothing. Failure retains a safe retry path for the same frozen collection and never falls back to the parent scope.
  • Success refreshes the report inventory and rendered detail from the confined sub-scope build. It does not open Source or change the main Index selection.

Package Eligibility

Sub-scope Import is opt-in per configured collection. Analysis/Tags is the first consumer; removing the current blanket blocker must not make every configured sub-scope importable.

For an opted-in sub-scope:

package profile supports_docs_review supports_return_import
document-content true true
document-tree false false

Trusted metadata must retain the exact scope, sub_scope, profile, selected_doc_ids, and prepared source-version map. Returned rows must equal the complete prepared ID set. Missing, extra, duplicate, malformed, cross-collection, or capability-invalid records block the whole package.

Existing sub-scope packages prepared under SRR-1 remain review-only because their trusted metadata says supports_return_import: false. They require regeneration after SRR-2; there is no metadata migration or compatibility fallback.

Canonical Apply Contract

  • Every returned ID must still identify one existing document in the frozen configured child collection. SRR-2 is overwrite-only: it does not create, delete, move, or rename documents.
  • The configured collection remains flat. Non-empty returned hierarchy fields block Import rather than inventing or mutating parent_id.
  • Returned title, summary, and document content may update. Canonical collection metadata not owned by the package—such as group, ui_status, viewable, immutable doc_id, and added_date—is preserved.
  • Trusted prepared source versions are compared with current canonical sources during preview and again immediately before apply. Any stale target refreshes or blocks the plan and requires a new confirmation.
  • Preview is write-free and exposes the complete planned document set. There is no record selection, skip, create/overwrite choice, or partial confirmation.
  • Apply precomputes and validates every target before entering one confined write boundary. A source-write or rebuild failure restores the pre-apply source snapshot and reports no successful Import.
  • The grouped terminal result is returned and presented directly. The shared scope and sub-scope package workflow creates no standalone result document, results/ directory, result-path response field, or result-specific log.
  • The existing sub-scope write/rebuild owner performs the confined projection follow-through. Parent Index, Recent, global search, and other collections remain unchanged.

Ownership

  • The SSO-1 sub-scope contribution retains ownership of the toolbar button, availability projection, and explicit mounted-collection request.
  • The document-report management host retains validation of that request and lazy loading of the shared Import workflow.
  • Existing returned-package listing and trusted validation remain the package discovery and whole-package identity owners.
  • The document-package Import planner and normalized ImportContent boundary are extended with an explicit sub-scope collection target; a second parser or parallel document mutation model is not added.
  • The sub-scope source write/rebuild service owns confined apply, rollback, and generated follow-through.
  • The ordinary Docs Import modal, top-level collection planner, and Docs Review route retain their current behavior.

Boundary

In scope:

  • explicit per-sub-scope returned-package Import opt-in;
  • exact-collection package listing, preview, confirmation, apply, and result;
  • a returned-package source type inside the existing 📥 Import report workflow, still independent of checkbox selection;
  • strict package capability, identity, membership, and flatness validation;
  • overwrite-only title, summary, and content updates;
  • stale-source revalidation and all-or-nothing source/rebuild behavior;
  • retirement of the unused standalone result artefact across the shared scope and sub-scope package workflow;
  • confined report refresh and focused service, module, route, and realistic acceptance evidence.

Not in scope:

  • Docs Review Save, Import, or query-string handoff;
  • public Import controls or local-service access;
  • ordinary HTML, DOCX, Markdown, text, or media Import redesign;
  • top-level package target, planning, or apply redesign;
  • document creation, deletion, hierarchy, moves, doc_id changes, or partial package apply;
  • Tag Registry reads, link repair, title synchronization, or group inference;
  • automatically enabling other sub-scopes; or
  • compatibility support for SRR-1 review-only package metadata.

Delivery Tracker

Current state: SRR-2.3 complete. SRR-2 is closed with realistic Analysis/Tags acceptance and current durable Docs Import documentation.

Review rule: complete one phase, record exact evidence, and stop for review before the next phase.

[x] SRR-2.0 — Freeze Eligibility And Exact Target

  • [x] Add explicit collection opt-in and importable sub-scope package projection without weakening false / true validation.
  • [x] Extend trusted listing and request validation with exact { scope, sub_scope }; retain fail-closed legacy behavior.

SRR-2.0 implementation and evidence

  • supports_return_import is now a strict boolean child-collection policy that defaults to false when omitted. Analysis/Tags is the only checked-config opt-in. Effective package capability is the conjunction of that policy and the profile capability: document-content projects true / true for Analysis/Tags, while document-tree remains false / false and unopted children remain true / false.
  • Dry-run results, written export metadata, external context, and returned listing records share that effective capability. Existing SRR-1 packages retain their stored supports_return_import: false and are blocked as review-only until regenerated.
  • GET /docs/packages/returned retains its scope-only Docs Review listing. An explicit scope plus sub_scope request first resolves one configured, opted-in child and then requires return-Import capability, exact trusted child provenance, supported profile, complete prepared membership, and current collection membership. Blank, unknown, unopted, mismatched, legacy, invalid-capability, and review-only inputs fail closed.
  • Focused Python evidence passed 155 tests with one environment-dependent loopback test skipped. The exercised surfaces cover checked and fixture scope config, package config/export/metadata/context, returned parsing and listing, ordinary and collection Import regressions, exact managed targets, public runtime isolation, source-config settings, and existing sub-scope ordinary Import.
  • Explicit Python lint passed for the thirteen changed source and test modules. JSON parsing and repository diff whitespace validation passed. The focused sensitive-value scan found only checklist prose and ordinary internal token wording.
  • The ordinary Import source registry deliberately still classifies every returned sub-scope package as unavailable. No package planner, canonical write, rebuild, rollback, browser chooser, public asset, or Docs Review mutation path was added at this checkpoint.
  • Independent final diff review found and corrected one exact-target leak before acceptance: returned parsing had validated child membership but still built its diagnostic current-source context from the parent scope. It now loads the frozen child collection, and focused assertions prove both returned records resolve there. The completed review found no second policy owner, inferred capability fallback, child-to-parent target fallback, compatibility alias, public capability projection, or evidence that the current documentation or explicit Python lint boundary is insufficient.

Checkpoint / review gate: eligibility projection and exact import-capable package discovery are ready; do not begin SRR-2.1 without review.

[x] SRR-2.1 — Plan And Apply The Whole Package

  • [x] Reuse normalized document-package planning for the exact flat collection with overwrite-only field ownership and stale-source validation.
  • [x] Apply every planned source and confined rebuild or restore the complete pre-apply snapshot.

SRR-2.1 implementation and evidence

  • Exact child requests can now classify an explicitly import-enabled returned package without exposing sub-scope packages through the ordinary global staged-source listing. Planning freezes the resolved managed collection, loads only its validated direct sources, and passes that target through the existing normalized collection and per-document planners.
  • Child package plans are overwrite-only. Missing targets cannot allocate identities or become creates, non-empty returned hierarchy blocks the whole package, and returned package assets remain unsupported. Returned title, summary, and content can change while canonical group, ui_status, viewable, doc_id, added_date, and other collection-owned front matter remain intact.
  • Trusted source_last_updated membership and non-blank values are required for the complete prepared set. Preview compares every prepared version with the current exact child sources; confirmed apply recomputes the whole plan and rechecks the trusted metadata digest. The confined write owner also compares the byte snapshot inside the write boundary so a final concurrent change returns a reconfirmation plan without overwriting that edit.
  • Confirmed apply precomputes every overwrite, snapshots every exact source, and enters the existing sub-scope write/rebuild boundary once. That owner now restores every source byte and performs a confined recovery rebuild after either a source-write or projection-build failure. The result records zero successful writes after rollback and includes explicit rollback state.
  • Focused service evidence passed 220 tests with one environment-dependent loopback test skipped. It covers ordinary and collection Import, returned package parsing and services, source formats and listings, exact managed targets, scope config, sub-scope rebuild ownership, stale reconfirmation, flat metadata preservation, a final write-boundary race, second-write failure, and confined rebuild failure.
  • Explicit Python lint passed for the nine changed source and test modules. Python compilation, repository whitespace validation, and a focused sensitive-value scan passed; its matches were existing path-sanitization fixtures, semantic/media token identifiers, and checklist prose.
  • Independent diff review removed a duplicate exact-child inventory loader in favour of the existing source-model owner and closed a watcher-suppression gap across snapshot restoration and the recovery rebuild. The completed review found no child-to-parent fallback, create or partial apply path, second parser, public runtime change, ordinary top-level package behavior change, or report UI work. SRR-2.2 remains unstarted.

Checkpoint / review gate: exact package planning and all-or-nothing canonical apply are ready; do not begin SRR-2.2 without review.

[x] SRR-2.2 — Extend Report Import

  • [x] Add trusted returned-package discovery and chooser state to the existing 📥 Import workflow without a second report button, and preserve Prepare package… checked-ID behavior.
  • [x] Move reviewed package plan, confirmation, result, and retry states into one shared sequential modal used by both scope-level and sub-scope Import, with only Cancel and Confirm import in its confirmation footer.

SRR-2.2 implementation and evidence

  • The existing report 📥 Import action still freezes one explicit mounted { scope, sub_scope } collection and lazily opens the shared Import modal. Its ordinary staged-document listing now loads alongside the exact trusted GET /docs/packages/returned listing; a package-listing failure leaves ordinary sources available instead of widening or replacing that workflow.
  • Returned listing records are accepted only when trusted scope, sub-scope, and supports_return_import: true match the frozen collection. The package mode shows filename, configured collection label, and document count, starts with no child package selected, and clears remembered package choice whenever the report destination is set again.
  • Successful package preview now closes the chooser lifecycle without restoring focus, then opens one shared Confirm package import modal for both scope-level and child targets. The complete plan scrolls independently of its fixed action row. Confirmation exposes only Cancel and Confirm import; there is no Back action. Cancel closes both steps, writes nothing, and returns focus to the initiating Import control.
  • The existing whole-package controller now carries the exact child target through preview, confirmation, refreshed-plan, apply, and result validation. Confirmed apply includes the trusted metadata digest. Cancel sends no apply; request or rollback failure retains the reviewed plan and confirmation for a same-target retry. Only a completed exact result reaches report refresh; a post-commit refresh failure exposes a refresh-only retry and never posts the package apply again.
  • Completed package Import refreshes the mounted child manifest with no-store, reprojects the list in place, and refreshes an active exact detail when present. It does not write report URL state, select a package record as a document target, open Source, or touch the main Index selection.
  • Five focused browser-module checks passed for the collection controller, ordinary/package Import, sequential modal focus, managed sub-scope report, and UI Workbench route. They cover both scope and child package targets, exactly one visible modal, fixed Cancel / Confirm import actions, no Back, cancel-without-apply, focus return, failed-apply retry, immutable confirmed identity, refresh-only post-commit recovery, exact result projection, in-place report refresh, inactive selection, and unchanged checked-ID Prepare package… behavior.
  • The shared package result now remains only in the terminal workflow response and normal application activity. The unused Markdown result writer, report_path response and activity plumbing, modal label, results/ staging exception, single-purpose shared renderer, tests, and current-state documentation were removed for both scope and sub-scope package Import.
  • A rendered local Analysis/Tags preview of 20260730-185610-documents-document-content.jsonl showed its complete two-record collision plan and both confirmation actions at the initial viewport without scrolling the plan. Cancel closed the workflow; no realistic confirm/apply was performed.
  • Focused Python evidence passed 46 tests covering collection planning/apply, source listing, child ordinary Import, and public/static runtime boundaries. The maintained Docs Viewer lint scope passed for 124 Python and 132 JavaScript files; explicit lint also passed for the four changed Python smoke modules and changed Workbench registry. Repository whitespace validation passed.
  • Final diff review retained one report Import control and two sequential modal lifecycles, not nested dialogs. It found no package fallback to parent scope, implicit document choice, public Import registration, Docs Review mutation, Prepare package target change, or service/parser change. At this checkpoint no realistic package apply had been performed; SRR-2.3 owned that acceptance.

Checkpoint / review gate: the shared package workflow now owns explicit scope or exact-child choice, sequential plan confirmation, retry, and confined report refresh; do not begin SRR-2.3 without review.

[x] SRR-2.3 — Verify And Accept

  • [x] Prove exact collection targeting, package/canonical staleness, cross-collection rejection, flat metadata preservation, rollback, and unchanged top-level/public behavior with focused fixtures.
  • [x] Preview and confirm one realistic regenerated Analysis/Tags package, then inspect the canonical sources and confined report projection.

SRR-2.3 acceptance

  • Focused acceptance passed 36 tests covering exact child plan/apply, package and canonical staleness, trusted metadata change, final write-boundary races, source-write and confined-rebuild rollback, flat metadata ownership, ordinary child Import, top-level collection behavior, exact importable package listing, and public runtime isolation.
  • The maintained Docs Viewer lint boundary passed for 124 Python and 132 JavaScript files. The focused collection browser smoke passed after the standalone result artefact was retired, and repository whitespace validation passed.
  • Trusted package 20260730-185610-documents-document-content.jsonl identified export ds_20260730T175610Z, exact target analysis/tags, return-Import and review capability, and exactly d-20260727-225608-579c27 plus d-20260727-225608-b5e4f7.
  • The realistic confirmation completed at 2026-07-30T18:34:17Z with zero creates, two overwrites, zero failures, completed confined generation, and no rollback. Both overwrite events named the exact Analysis/Tags source paths; no parent rebuild or fallback target was used.
  • Canonical absence and alienation match the returned bodies and retain their immutable IDs, original added_date, blank parent_id, group: theme, and canonical viewability. Their child by-id projections and manage-manifest rows match the accepted sources; parent Index, Recent, global search, and unrelated public surfaces remain outside the mutation boundary.
  • Docs Import, Docs Import Architecture, endpoint, and import-owner documents describe the shipped direct terminal result with no separate result document or result-specific log.

Completion Gate

Met. One explicitly import-enabled returned sub-scope package was chosen from the owning report, revalidated against the exact prepared and current collection, applied completely after one confirmation, and reflected by the confined report rebuild with no parent-scope, public, Docs Review, or partial-write side effect.
